In summary, our research is concerned with

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cerebral metabolic and circulatory effects of homocystine-induced seizures are similar to those seen in other forms of experimentally induced seizures.

homocysteines induced seizures in the rat are associated with a rise in CBF and CMRO2, and with perturbations of cerebral metabolites, including accumulation of ammonia, which may contribute to changes in amino acid concentrations.
the metabolic perturbation during seizures is due to both the induced seizure and the injected homocystine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the metabolic and circulatory perturbations occurring during homocysteic-induced seizures are qualitatively similar, but quantitatively more severe, than those occurring during electroconvulsive shock (ECS).
the metabolic changes during sustained seizures are qualitatively similar in rats and humans.
during sustained seizures in the rat, cerebral energy reserves are markedly perturbed, with depletion of phosphocreatine, accumulation of lactate and excessive formation of glyceraldehyde phosphate.

homocysteic acid is a potent convulsant, and it is possible that homocysteinemia may play a role in epilepsy in humans.
